learnings.question: Which economist first articulated, in 1971, the idea that an abundance of information creates a scarcity of attention?
learnings.learning: Economist Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of its recipients.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What single question does one blogger's automated daily script ask to decide whether a YouTube video earns a spot in his personal, algorithm-free content feed?
options: Does this video have more than 10,000 views?
Was this video uploaded in the last 24 hours?
Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
Is this video under 20 minutes long?
learnings.learning: Instead of trusting social media algorithms, one can build a personal content engine: a script that pulls videos from hand-picked trusted channels and filters them with AI by asking a single tailored question about personal benefit.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century researcher demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus proved that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is why re-reading notes is far less effective than being quizzed on them.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term describes the brain's tendency to stop retaining information once it has been written down or saved externally, such as on a phone or in notes?
learnings.learning: Psychologists call it the "Performance Paradox" of Cognitive Offloading: the moment we write something down or save it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to let it go, which is part of why we no longer remember phone numbers.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, what is the primary purpose of breaking project work into short, iterative cycles called Sprints?
options: To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To reduce the number of team members needed
To eliminate the need for a product backlog
To increase the overall length of the project
learnings.learning: Scrum is an agile approach that breaks work into smaller, iterative cycles called Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments, with each sprint following a Plan -> Build -> Test -> Review cycle.

learnings.question: Which Scrum artifact visually tracks the remaining work in a Sprint and helps a team see whether it's on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is one of Scrum's three core artifacts; it visualizes a Sprint's progress by showing remaining work and helping the team track whether it is on schedule.

learnings.question: In a common Islamic framework of life's purpose, which three core roles are humans said to fulfill?
options: Seeking wealth, pursuing knowledge, and raising a family
Worshipping Allah, serving as steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter
learnings.learning: Life's purpose is often framed around three primary roles: worshiping Allah, serving as a steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the eternal Hereafter through conscious choices and accountability.

learnings.question: What Arabic term, used in the Quran, refers to humanity's role as steward or caretaker of the Earth?
learnings.learning: The term "khalifah" refers to humanity's role as caretaker of Allah's creation, a responsibility that goes beyond personal actions to preserving faith and fostering unity within the community.

learnings.question: What moral lesson is conveyed by the teaching that a person will "see" even an atom's weight of the good or evil they have done?
options: No deed, however small, is wasted — every action carries a consequence
Only major sins are punished in the afterlife
Good deeds automatically cancel out all evil deeds
Intentions matter more than the actions themselves
learnings.learning: The teaching that whoever does an atom's weight of good or evil will see it reinforces that in divine justice, no good effort is wasted and every deed, no matter how small, is accounted for.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents a device being almost completely powered down, offering the greatest power savings but the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power management state, where the device is almost completely powered down; it is used for the longest periods of inactivity and has the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Within the PCIe L1 power state, what distinguishes the deeper substate L1.2 from L1.0?
options: L1.2 shuts the device off completely, identically to L2
L1.2 powers down more components for greater power savings but a longer wake-up time
L1.2 is a fully active, high-performance state
L1.2 has no effect on wake-up latency compared to L1.0
learnings.learning: PCIe's L1 state has substates L1.1 and L1.2 that go deeper than L1.0 by powering down additional electrical circuits of the main link, trading greater power savings for increased wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what is the key distinction between "Qada'" and "Qadr"?
options: Qada' is prayer while Qadr is fasting
Qada' is the actual unfolding of events in life, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal preordained knowledge and plan
They are two different names for the exact same concept
Qada' refers to the Hereafter while Qadr refers to worldly life
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in life, shaped by one's actions and decisions, while Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal knowledge of everything that will ever happen.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Per a hadith recorded in Jami at-Tirmidhi, what does Allah do when a Muslim sincerely supplicates (makes dua) for something permissible?
options: Allah only responds during the last third of the night
Allah defers all answers until the Day of Judgment
Allah either grants the request or wards off an equivalent amount of evil from them
Allah grants it only if the supplication is repeated 100 times
learnings.learning: A hadith in Jami at-Tirmidhi states that there is no Muslim who supplicates to Allah with any permissible request except that Allah either grants it to them or turns away from them an equivalent amount of evil.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In a data analysis applying the 80/20 Pareto Principle to word frequency in the Quran, what percentage of the total text did the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Applying the Pareto Principle to word frequency in the Quran, the top 20 most repeated words only accumulate to about 20.83% of the total text, not the 80% the 80/20 rule might predict.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What term refers to the small diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate which vowel sound to use; without them, reading Arabic text can be ambiguous since identical spellings can carry different pronunciations.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
